spec: Layer 8 §2.2 rule 2 the node-state store key (§2.7 S1 KeyProvider::key_for; §3 J5: a key-derivation tag, never a signing tag)
description: node_state_key = BLAKE2b-256(key = store_secret (32 B), data = '111/node-state/v1' ‖ NodeId (32 B)) — RFC 7693 keyed mode, 32-byte digest: the KDF of ../store-kdf.json under the node-state tag (mesh111 keys::derive_tagged_key, reached through KeyProvider::key_for); handed to SQLCipher as the raw key literal x'<64 hex>' for node/state.db (no PBKDF2 at open). 'kdf_input' is the keyed hash's data, tag ‖ NodeId (49 B). The inputs are ../store-kdf.json's cases in its order, so each node_state_key stands beside the store_key of the same inputs and differs from it. store_secret is the identity holder's Mode S secret (Sealer::store_secret); it is an input here, never a key on disk.
provenance: Generated by mesh111 keys::tests::layer8::write_layer8_vectors (ignored) over the inputs of ../store-kdf.json. layer8_files_match_generation fails on a missing file or any byte of drift; node_state_kdf_vectors re-derives every case through derive_tagged_key and KeyProvider::key_for (Mode S) and requires the two answers computed independently with Python hashlib.blake2b(b'111/node-state/v1' + node_id, key=store_secret, digest_size=32) verbatim; crosscheck.py's layer8/ section re-derives every field from Layer 8 §2.2 rule 2 alone.
